newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - IVAN WONG COMMENTS ON MALAYSIAN PALM OIL.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - IVAN WONG COMMENTS ON MALAYSIAN PALM OIL.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 - Our final estimate on CPO production in July remains unchanged at 823,000 tonnes or about 4.5 percent higher than month earlier. Production in Peninsular Malaysia is estimated to have increased nearly 5 percent. The performance of major producers mostly ranged from two to 10 percent higher. In East Malaysia production ranged widely from down 5 percent to up 10 percent with declines reported by estates/mills which experienced dry weather and poor oil extraction rates (OER). However weather has improved since early last week and should have a beneficial impact on OER and production.

Feedback received from Indonesia meanwhile indicated production in the country rose strongly by an estimated 13 percent in July,, up from around 3 percent in June. Indonesian production in January-June is estimated to have expanded 9 percent on an annual basis. Our estimate on palm oil offtake (include exports) and end-July stocks of palm oil at 805,000 tonnes also remain unchanged. However, CPO stocks are lowered to 450,000 tonnes while PPO stocks are scaled upward to an estimated 355,000 tonnes.

This reflected entirely the situation in East Malaysia where stocks of CPO were drawn down to meet active refinery requirements and brisk export shipments schedule in late July/ early August. In contrast to the robust demand for palm oil, offtake of PKO was down slightly. Consequently, stocks of PK/PKO rose by some 20,000 tonnes to an estimated 160,000 tonnes, oil basis. Crushers struggled to break even because of weak demand for PKO and PKM. PKO also faced keen competition from Philippine and Indonesian exports of CNO.

Since July 11 domestic CPO price had trended strongly upward as the ringgit assumed a continuous downtrend. As of yesterday, the ringgit had slumped to 2.7860 on renewed speculative attacks, down 11.2 percent from 2.5045 on July 11. During this same period, CPO futures surged 10.7 percent or 121 ringgit to 1,249 ringgit, basis the active third-month contract. Since the beginning of this month the ringgit's decline of 6.1 percent had bolstered CPO price by 7 percent or 82 ringgit. The commodity's strength was also underlined by its present good fundamentals which enabled CPO to benefit fully from the ringgit's fall.

Export market price in US dollar terms for RBD palm/olein were practically unchanged and very much in line with the world price of competing SBO and RSO which had remained relatively flat. The USDA meanwhile estimated a 1997/98 US SB crop of 2.744 billion bullish or two percent higher than the month-ago estimate. Boosted by a 10.4 percent expansion in planted acreage to 70.9 million acre and a prospective 4.5 percent rise in yield to 39.3 bullion/acre, this year's crop represents a big increase of 15.2 percent over the 2.382 billion bullish harvested in 1996/97.

End season stocks of SB was projected to recover to 305 million bullish from 125 million bullish estimated at the end of this season. 1997/98 ending stocks of SBO were projected to rise to 1,795 million LBS from 1,625 million LBS this season.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
